title: Supplied Allegation of Coordinated ICE Raids and Mass Arrests
description_short: Supplied allegation: coordinated ICE raids and mass arrests in major cities
description_medium: The supplied entry alleges that ICE coordinated raids across major U.S. cities on July 21, 2025, producing thousands of arrests and civil-rights violations. It also alleges that citizens and permanent residents were caught up in the operation. The packet does not identify the operation or corroborate its scope, date, arrests, or excessive-force claims; this draft is not publication-eligible.
description_long: The supplied record alleges that a coordinated ICE operation took place on July 21, 2025, across several major U.S. cities. It says the raids produced thousands of arrests, swept up citizens and permanent residents along with people targeted for immigration enforcement, and involved civil-rights violations and excessive force. These are allegations from the frozen entry, not established findings. The packet names no city, operation, arrest total, person, court case, eyewitness, or contemporaneous report that would let a reader verify the claims. A Guardian data analysis published two days later reported that June average daily ICE arrests were 268% higher than in June 2024 and described separate large-scale Los Angeles raids. That context does not document this specific July 21 operation or confirm the claimed arrests, status of those detained, or use of force. The event's exact date, scope, affected people, and alleged conduct remain unverified. This copy is internal only until source evidence identifies the operation and supports its central claims.

source_fact_map.fact: A Guardian analysis reported June average daily ICE arrests were 268% higher than June 2024; this is broad context and does not establish the supplied July 21 operation.
source_fact_map.quote: In June this year, average daily arrests were up 268% compared with June 2024.
source_fact_map.source_excerpt:
A Guardian analysis of the dataset found:

- In June this year, average daily arrests were up 268% compared with June 2024.

- Ice is increasingly targeting any and all unauthorized immigrants, including people who have no criminal records.

title: Supplied Allegation of FBI Leak Probes Targeting Critical Journalists
description_short: Supplied allegation: FBI leak probes targeted journalists critical of Trump
description_medium: The supplied record alleges that the FBI under newly appointed director Kash Patel opened leak investigations in February 2025 against journalists and outlets critical of Donald Trump. It describes the action as a probe into sources behind coverage and alleges a chilling effect on the press. The packet verifies Patel's start date only; it does not establish the investigation, targets, or retaliatory motive.
description_long: The supplied entry alleges that in February 2025 the FBI, under Kash Patel, opened leak investigations targeting journalists and news organizations because of critical coverage of Donald Trump. It describes the probes as searches for government sources behind reporting on the Russia investigation, January 6, and Trump's business dealings, and says press-freedom groups condemned the action. Those details remain allegations in the supplied record. The packet names no investigated journalist or outlet, case number, FBI announcement, court filing, or direct evidence tying an investigation to unfavorable coverage. The FBI's biography states that Patel became director on February 20, 2025, but that official record does not corroborate the alleged probes. Search results located later reporting about an internal FBI inquiry into leakers and a separate March leak-investigation announcement by the Director of National Intelligence; neither establishes this specific February FBI action or its asserted motive. The targets, date, scope, and press-group response remain unverified. This draft is internal only and cannot be published as fact.

original_title: Trump Ends Community Development Block Grant Program
blockers: The frozen record asserts that the Trump administration terminated CDBG in March 2025. The FY2025 stopgap appropriations law signed March 15 maintained $3.3 billion in CDBG formula funding, and HUD's May 13 FY2025 allocation page lists CDBG among its full-year formula programs. No supplied counterpart or source located documents a separate March termination. The supported action is continuation of funding, not termination; converting that continuation into a harmful-impact card would replace the asserted event with a different, non-harmful event. The termination claim is contradicted and no publication-eligible harmful event survives this repair.

source_fact_map.fact: The March 2025 continuing resolution maintained $3.3 billion in FY2025 formula funding for CDBG, contradicting the claim that the program ended in March.
source_fact_map.quote: The bill maintains $3.3 billion in formula funding for the Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) program
source_fact_map.source_excerpt: The bill maintains $3.3 billion in formula funding for the Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) program; the funding decrease can be solely attributed to the loss of “earmarks,” or congressionally requested funding for community development projects. The CR preserves the $100 million set-aside within the CDBG program for the PRO-Housing competition, which provides state and local governments with incentives to adopt less restrictive zoning and land use laws that allow for the development of more affordable housing.

source_fact_map.fact: HUD's FY2025 allocation page states the fiscal-year budget was enacted and its full-year formula allocations include CDBG.
source_fact_map.source_excerpt: The Fiscal Year (FY) 2025budget for the Department of Housing and Urban Development has been enacted. This spreadsheet provides full-year allocations for the Office of Community Planning and Development's (CPD) formula programs:Community Development Block Grants (CDBG); CDBG Recovery Housing Program (RHP); HOME Investment Partnerships Program (HOME); Emergency Solutions Grants (ESG); Housing Opportunities for Persons With AIDS (HOPWA); and Housing Trust Fund (HTF). Content current as of May 13, 2025.

research_attempts.result: Results distinguish a May budget request proposing CDBG elimination and separate affordable-housing contract cancellations from the enacted March FY2025 funding law, which maintained CDBG formula funding.

impact_proposal.confidence_reason: The supplied termination claim is contradicted by the enacted FY2025 funding law and HUD allocation record; no supported harmful event remains to score.
impact_proposal.rationale: The central claim that CDBG ended in March is not supported and conflicts with evidence that funding continued. The sources establish continuation, not a distinct harmful action suitable for this impact record.
impact_proposal.basis: Frozen entry alleges March 2025 termination of CDBG; NLIHC and HUD evidence show FY2025 formula funding and allocations continued.
impact_proposal.notes: Exclusion candidate; no impact score assigned to the contradiction or to the non-harmful funding continuation.
